subject: Post-call: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Steve Ramos <sramos@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-01-10T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management

Thanks again for the time today, Steve — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference into FintechCo's transactions pipeline (embeddings + reranker + streaming generation).
- Main integration concerns: SDK setup, auth & key management, routing between prod/stage, structured output/tool-calling for transactions, and per-model quotas.

Redwood recommendations (high level):
1) Auth options we support: API keys (server-to-server), OAuth 2.0 client_credentials (for service-to-service with short-lived tokens), and JWT bearer with JWKS (for customer-signed tokens).
2) Key management: we recommend service accounts per environment (prod/stage), store keys in your KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault), and rotate keys on a schedule (default 30 days, configurable). Redwood supports key-rotation-safe public key discovery via jwks_url and can accept short-lived tokens issued by your STS.
3) SDK setup: our SDKs (Node/Python/Go) include helpers for token refresh, automatic key rotation handling, and built-in retry/backoff for transient failures.
4) Routing & quotas: you can route requests by header or token scope to different model variants (cost vs latency), and apply per-token/model quotas from the control plane.

Attachments: redwood-api-authn-guide.pdf — short guide + sample flows. Also linking our docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/api/authentication

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive where Dev (solutions eng) walks through the token exchange flow and SDK examples.
- Please share your constraints: SSO provider (Okta/Azure AD), KMS provider, required rotation window, and whether client-side apps need direct access (i.e., public clients).

Can we do Monday 1/13 at 10am PT for the tech walkthrough? I’ll have Dev on the call to go through the architecture diagram and sample code.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0118

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few follow-ups from our security team: 

1) We use Okta for SSO and AWS KMS for key storage. We’d prefer to issue our own JWTs for service accounts and have Redwood accept them (JWT Bearer flow). Does Redwood support JWKS endpoint validation and key rollover?
2) Rotation cadence: security policy suggests rotating signing keys every 14–30 days. Can Redwood handle overlapping keys (i.e., accept current + previous key for 48 hours during rotation)?
3) For client apps: we do not want long-lived API keys embedded in mobile clients. OAuth 2 client_credentials or a token exchange flow would be preferable. Can you share a sample for client_credentials + token exchange with Redwood?

Also, we’ll need sample code for issuing scoped tokens (scopes for embeddings vs. generation/reranker) and enforcement of per-model quotas at request time.

Nicole and I will join the Monday 10am PT slot if that works — can you confirm the agenda?

—Steve
Steve Ramos
Head of Integrations | FintechCo
sramos@fintechco.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>
To: Steve Ramos <sramos@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management

Hi Steve — thanks for the details, this is all doable. High-level architecture proposal (summary):

- Service accounts per environment (prod/stage/dev). Each service account has a keypair managed in your AWS KMS.
- FintechCo issues short-lived JWTs (signed by KMS) with a claims set: {sub, iss, aud, exp, scope, kid}. Redwood will validate JWTs against your jwks_url (or accept introspection if you prefer).
- Overlapping keys: Redwood supports key rollover windows — we recommend publishing the new key to JWKS and keeping the previous key for 48–72 hours; our token validator will accept both during the window.
- Rotation cadence: default suggestions: 30 days for signing keys, 7 days for access tokens; we can accommodate 14-day rotation if required.
- Scopes & RBAC: include scopes like "embed:read", "model:generate", "rerank:invoke" in the token. Redwood enforces scopes at the route level and can tie quotas to scopes or service-account IDs.

Sample integration snippets (we'll demo live):
- OAuth2 client_credentials: your backend exchanges client_id/secret for short-lived token issued by your IdP, then calls Redwood with the token in Authorization: Bearer <token>.
- If you prefer API keys for internal batch jobs, use rotated API keys stored in KMS and rotate via our control plane API (we can automate key rotation via a webhook).

Attachment: rdw-authn-architecture-diagram.png — shows token exchange, jwks discovery, and routing per-scope.

Agenda proposal for Monday 1/13 10am PT (30 mins):
- 10:00–10:05: Quick intros & goals (Marissa/Steve)
- 10:05–10:15: Architecture walkthrough (Dev)
- 10:15–10:25: SDK/sample code & demo - token exchange, JWKS validation (live)
- 10:25–10:30: Q/A and next steps (decide PoC scope + timelines)

If that looks good I’ll share a short sample repo link prior to the call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
